seo.title: Help for people without housing in Miami - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help in Miami for people without housing: shelter access, meals, showers, health care, benefits, work, documents and specialist support.

page.heading: Miami — help for people without housing
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire or medical emergency: 911 Homeless Helpline: 1-877-994-HELP (4357) or 305-375-CARE (2273) Mental health or suicide crisis: 988; community services: 211 County information: 311 or 305-468-5900
page.notice: Beds, hours, eligibility and supplies can change. Call before travelling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, appointment, payment, treatment or job on the same day.
page.intro: If you do not have a safe place tonight, start with the Miami-Dade Homeless Helpline. Shelter intake is coordinated: do not assume that arriving at a shelter will get you a bed. Say where you are, whether children or violence are involved, and whether you have a health condition, disability, pregnancy, pet or transportation problem.
page.footer: No Home Help — free, static information without tracking.

entries.title: 911 — immediate danger
entries.description:
Call: 911.
Use for serious illness or injury, breathing trouble, overdose, fire, violence or immediate danger. Give your location first; an intersection or landmark is useful if you do not have an address.
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue contact information

entries.title: 988 — mental health and suicide crisis
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, 24 hours.
Free, confidential crisis support in English and Spanish, with interpretation for other languages. If there is an immediate medical danger, call 911.
988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

entries.title: 211 Miami — community services
entries.description:
Call: 211, 24 hours.
Ask for the nearest open food program, crisis support, family help, health care or other social service. Verify the address and intake time before leaving.
211 Miami

entries.title: 311 — Miami-Dade County services
entries.description:
Call: 311 or 305-468-5900. The phone service supports English, Spanish and Haitian Creole.
Use for County services, library locations, weather information, Animal Services and a request for homeless outreach. An outreach request can use an intersection or general area instead of a street address.
Miami-Dade 311

entries.title: Extreme heat
entries.description:
Miami-Dade libraries, selected parks and government buildings act as cooling sites. Check the live list because a location may close for renovation or have limited hours.
Go to shade or air conditioning, drink water and call 911 for confusion, fainting, seizures or other signs of heatstroke. Homeless outreach teams may distribute water and cooling supplies during alerts.
Current cooling sites

entries.title: Cold-weather shelter activation
entries.description:
When the County activates its cold-weather plan, extra shelter is coordinated through the Homeless Trust. Call 1-877-994-4357 for the current instructions.
Do not rely on a previous season's location. In medical danger from cold exposure, call 911.
Homeless Helpline weather information

entries.title: Miami-Dade Homeless Helpline — start here
entries.description:
Call: 1-877-994-HELP (4357) or 305-375-CARE (2273); Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
The Helpline assesses people who are homeless or at risk and connects them with outreach or the coordinated shelter system. Shelter placement depends on assessment and an available, suitable bed.
After choosing a language: option 1 is for people at risk of homelessness, option 2 for domestic violence or trafficking, option 3 for veterans, option 4 for Miami Beach, and option 5 for other Miami-Dade locations.
Official Homeless Helpline instructions

entries.title: City of Miami Homeless Assistance Program
entries.description:
Outreach, assessment, shelter and housing referrals, transport help and connections to support services. Going in person does not guarantee a bed or payment.
City homeless assistance
entries.address: Walk-in: Stephen P. Clark Government Center, 111 NW 1st Street, 1st floor, Miami, FL 33128
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; information: 311 or 305-416-2080.

entries.title: Street outreach request
entries.description:
Call the Homeless Helpline during its hours. Outside those hours, call 311 and ask for homeless outreach. Give the person's location, clothing or other identifying details, immediate risks and whether the person agrees to speak with a team.
The County says an address is not required; an intersection or general area can be used. Outreach is not an emergency service, so call 911 for immediate danger.
How to request outreach

entries.title: Camillus House Day Center
entries.description:
Day services include meals, showers, clean clothing, mail, computers, help obtaining Florida identification, an employment specialist and access to health care.
Emergency shelter placement normally requires a Homeless Trust referral. Use the Homeless Helpline rather than travelling there expecting a bed.
Camillus House — need help
entries.address: Address: 1603 NW 7th Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Miami Rescue Mission — The Caring Place
entries.description:
Phone: 305-571-2211.
Provides shelter, meals, showers, laundry, case management, clinic access, education and job preparation. Call first and use the Homeless Helpline for coordinated shelter intake; a bed is not guaranteed.
Miami Rescue Mission location and services
entries.address: Address: 2020 NW 1st Avenue, Miami, FL 33127

entries.title: Lotus House — women, youth and children
entries.description:
Phone: 305-438-0556. Youth and people escaping domestic violence may email needshelter@lotushouse.org. — mailto:needshelter@lotushouse.org
Lotus House serves women, youth and children with shelter and support. Contact does not reserve a bed; for general shelter access, also call the Homeless Helpline.
Lotus House contact and shelter guidance
entries.address: Address: 217 NW 15th Street, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Families with minor children
entries.description:
Call the Homeless Helpline and explain the number and ages of all children, custody arrangements, pregnancy, medical needs and where the family can safely wait.
Ask what documents to bring, but do not delay a call because papers are missing. Placement depends on assessment and family-appropriate availability.
Current family access instructions

entries.title: Unaccompanied youth and young adults, ages 13–24
entries.description:
Call 1-877-994-4357 and ask for the youth access route. The County lists access partners including Camillus House, Lotus House, Citrus Health Network, Educate Tomorrow, Miami Bridge and Pridelines.
Say your age, whether you are alone, whether an adult is hurting or exploiting you, and whether you need a safe place tonight.
Youth access through the Homeless Helpline

entries.title: If there is no bed available
entries.description:
Ask for the next safe step, a day center, outreach follow-up and the best time to call again. Explain any health condition, disability, pregnancy, violence risk, child, older adult, pet or inability to travel.
Do not pay anyone who claims to sell a shelter bed. Keep a note of the date, time and number called. Use 911 for immediate danger.
Miami-Dade Homeless Trust

entries.title: Camillus House meals
entries.description:
The current help page lists meals Monday–Friday at 8:30 a.m. and an additional meal Tuesday and Thursday at 12:30 p.m. Times and capacity can change, so arrive early and confirm before a long trip.
Camillus House meal and day-service times
entries.address: Day Center: 1603 NW 7th Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Miami Rescue Mission meals
entries.description:
Phone: 305-571-2211.
The Mission provides weekday meals. Published times differ between current local directories, so call for the day's serving time before travelling.
The Caring Place — Miami services
entries.address: Address: 2020 NW 1st Avenue, Miami, FL 33127

entries.title: Missionaries of Charity of Mother Teresa
entries.description:
The current Camillus help directory lists a meal from 10:00–11:00 a.m. every day except Thursday. Confirm before travelling because community meal schedules can change.
Camillus House local food directory
entries.address: Address: 724 NW 17th Street, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Salvation Army Center of Hope food pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 305-456-5850; pantry: Tuesday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–noon.
The pantry provides a seven-day supply of groceries and essential items. Call about identification, household information and current stock.
Salvation Army Miami feeding programs
entries.address: Address: 1907 NW 38th Street, Miami, FL 33142

entries.title: Salvation Army Miami Citadel — Little Havana
entries.description:
Phone: 305-545-9164.
The Citadel distributes grocery bags on a recurring schedule. The official page describes distribution as biweekly but does not publish a fixed day, so call first.
Salvation Army food assistance
entries.address: Address: 911 W Flagler Street, Miami, FL 33130

entries.title: Matthew 25 Food Pantry — Catholic Charities
entries.description:
Phone: 305-964-7816.
First-time visitors must attend on a Wednesday or Thursday for intake and registration. Enrolled households may attend once monthly on scheduled Saturdays. Check the distribution calendar before travelling.
Matthew 25 Food Pantry registration
entries.address: Address: 14205 SW 142nd Avenue, Miami, FL 33186

entries.title: Care Resource Little Havana food pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 305-576-1234.
The health center has an on-site food pantry alongside medical, dental and pharmacy services. Call about pantry hours and eligibility before going.
Care Resource Little Havana
entries.address: Address: 1800 SW 1st Street, Miami, FL 33135

entries.title: Feeding South Florida — find a pantry
entries.description:
Miami-Dade client services: 954-518-1857.
Use the agency locator for a nearby partner pantry or ask about SNAP, WIC and TANF application help. Confirm the partner's hours, documents and ZIP-code rules before travelling.
Feeding South Florida agency finder

entries.title: When a listed food site is closed
entries.description:
Call 211 and ask for a food distribution open today near your current location. Miami-Dade also links current Farm Share and pantry calendars.
Bring bags if possible and ask whether the site requires registration, household information, proof of address or a vehicle.
Miami-Dade food assistance resources

categories.title: Showers, clothes, laundry, mail and internet

entries.title: Camillus House showers and clothing
entries.description:
Showers begin Monday–Friday at 6:30 a.m. The Day Center also lists clean clothing and other basic-needs help. Arrive early; service depends on daily capacity.
Camillus House basic-needs services
entries.address: Day Center: 1603 NW 7th Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Camillus House mail service
entries.description:
Mail service is listed Monday–Friday, 11:00 a.m.–noon. Ask how your name must appear, what identification is accepted and how long mail is held before using the address on an application.
Camillus House current service times
entries.address: Address: 1603 NW 7th Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Miami Rescue Mission showers and laundry
entries.description:
Community showers are listed Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 2:00–5:00 p.m. The site also provides laundry and clothing support. Call 305-571-2211 to confirm access and required items.
Miami Rescue Mission services
entries.address: Address: 2020 NW 1st Avenue, Miami, FL 33127

entries.title: Miami-Dade Public Library social services
entries.description:
Phone: 786-988-6816; email: socialservicesmail@mdpls.org. — mailto:socialservicesmail@mdpls.org
Ask about current library social-service hours and locations. Libraries can also provide a safe daytime space, public computers, internet and cooling during regular hours; local rules still apply.
County library social-service contact

entries.title: Main Library computers and workspace
entries.description:
The library and its CareerSource center offer technology and workspaces for job applications. Bring any library card or identification you have, but ask staff what is available if you have neither.
Main Library information
entries.address: Address: 101 W Flagler Street, Miami, FL 33130

categories.title: Health, mental health and substance use

entries.title: Camillus Health Concern — Good Shepherd Health Center
entries.description:
Appointments: 305-341-0152; main: 305-577-4840.
Primary care and behavioral health: Monday 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Tuesday–Wednesday 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.; Thursday–Friday 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Dental and dispensary hours are Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Camillus Health locations and hours
entries.address: Address: 336 NW 5th Street, Miami, FL 33128

entries.title: Camillus Health Clinic — Norwegian Cruise Line Campus
entries.description:
Primary and behavioral health care near the Camillus House campus. Listed hours are Monday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Tuesday–Wednesday 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Thursday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Call 305-341-0152 for an appointment and ask what documents or payment information to bring.
Camillus Health clinic contacts
entries.address: Address: 1545 NW 7th Avenue, 2nd floor, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Camillus Health at the Salvation Army
entries.description: Camillus Health outreach location
entries.address: Address: 1907 NW 38th Street, Suite 195, Miami, FL 33142
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–noon. Call 305-341-0152 before travelling.

entries.title: Jefferson Reaves Sr. Health Center
entries.description:
Phone: 786-466-4000; Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Wednesday 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Jackson Health primary care and social services. If uninsured, ask for a financial evaluation; reduced cost is based on an assessment, not automatic.
Jefferson Reaves Health Center
entries.address: Address: 1009 NW 5th Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Jackson Health financial assistance
entries.description:
Financial assessment: 305-585-6000.
Jackson provides emergency care regardless of ability to pay and has financial-assistance and sliding-fee processes for eligible patients. Ask for an assessment; residency, household, income and immigration criteria may apply.
Jackson Health financial assistance

entries.title: Care Resource Little Havana
entries.description:
Phone: 305-576-1234.
Medical, dental, behavioral-health, pharmacy and wellness services. A sliding-fee program is based on household size and income; Care Resource states that inability to pay does not by itself prevent care.
Care Resource sliding-fee information
entries.address: Address: 1800 SW 1st Street, Miami, FL 33135

entries.title: Mobile behavioral crisis support
entries.description:
Camillus Health crisis line: 800-435-7968, also written as 800-HELP-YOU.
For a behavioral-health crisis in Miami-Dade. For immediate violence, a medical emergency or danger to life, call 911; for nationwide crisis counselling, call or text 988.
Camillus Health emergency contacts

entries.title: Substance-use help through Camillus House
entries.description:
Camillus House lists an intervention and treatment program for people who are homeless and actively using substances. Start at the Day Center or ask the Homeless Helpline for a referral.
Do not stop alcohol, benzodiazepines or other dependence-forming drugs suddenly without medical advice. Call 911 for overdose, seizures or loss of consciousness.
Camillus House treatment access

entries.title: Pridelines sexual health and HIV services
entries.description:
Phone: 305-571-9601.
Confidential HIV testing, STI screening, PrEP and PEP navigation, wellness care and LGBTQ+-affirming support. Call for an appointment and the current testing location.
Pridelines contact and health services
entries.address: Miami Beach center: 1130 Washington Avenue, 1st floor, Miami Beach, FL 33139

entries.title: MyACCESS Florida — SNAP, cash and Medicaid
entries.description:
Customer service: 850-300-4323.
Use one application for SNAP food assistance, Temporary Cash Assistance, Medicaid and Refugee Assistance. Applying is free; each program has separate eligibility rules. Paper and community-partner applications are available if online access is difficult.
Florida public-assistance application

entries.title: Accion Community Resource Center
entries.description:
Phone: 305-545-2224; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
County resource center for referrals and applications involving food, utilities, housing stability, older adults, disability and family needs. Programs and funding vary; call first.
Miami-Dade Community Resource Centers
entries.address: Address: 970 SW 1st Street, 4th floor, Miami, FL 33130

entries.title: Culmer Community Resource Center
entries.description:
Phone: 305-438-4161; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Ask for benefits screening and current emergency-assistance or referral programs. Bring notices, identification and income information if available, but call even if some papers are missing.
County resource-center information
entries.address: Address: 1600 NW 3rd Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Homeless prevention and rapid rehousing
entries.description:
The City program can provide temporary rental or utility help to some low-income residents who are homeless or at documented risk. Eligibility, income limits, documentation and available funding apply.
Start with the Homeless Helpline or the City walk-in office. A notice, outreach referral or institutional discharge record may be requested; assistance is never guaranteed.
City prevention and rapid-rehousing rules

entries.title: Catholic Charities prevention and rapid rehousing
entries.description:
Phone: 305-573-3333.
The County lists rent, mortgage, utility, food-voucher and case-management help for eligible Miami-Dade residents who are homeless or at risk and can document hardship. Call before visiting; funding and eligibility change.
County rapid-rehousing listing
entries.address: Program address: 3620 NW 1st Avenue, Miami, FL 33127

entries.title: Check funding before relying on rental assistance
entries.description:
Miami-Dade's general rental and utility assistance page currently warns that several programs are on hold until funding becomes available. Do not sign a lease or promise payment based only on an application.
Ask the Homeless Helpline, City office or resource center which program is accepting applications today.
Current County assistance status

entries.title: CareerSource at the Main Library
entries.description:
Phone: 786-582-3013; Monday–Friday, 9:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m.
Employment help, résumé and interview preparation, employer connections, training information, computers and workspace for applications.
CareerSource Main Library center
entries.address: Address: 101 W Flagler Street, 1st floor, Miami, FL 33130

entries.title: CareerSource Little Havana
entries.description:
Phone: 305-442-6900; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Job search, training and workforce services. Call about orientation, identification and whether an appointment is required.
CareerSource South Florida locations
entries.address: Address: 5040 NW 7th Street, Suite 200, Miami, FL 33126

entries.title: Camillus House employment specialist
entries.description:
Ask for the employment specialist and computer access. Staff may help with a résumé, job search and referrals while other housing or document needs are addressed.
Camillus House employment help
entries.address: Day Center: 1603 NW 7th Avenue, Miami, FL 33136

entries.title: Miami Rescue Mission education and work preparation
entries.description:
Programs include education, computer-lab access, vocational development and job preparation for eligible participants. Call 305-571-2211 and ask how to enter the relevant program.
The Caring Place programs
entries.address: Address: 2020 NW 1st Avenue, Miami, FL 33127

entries.title: Employment while replacing documents
entries.description:
Tell CareerSource or a day-center employment specialist if missing identification, a Social Security card, phone, address, clothing or transportation is blocking work. Ask to make a written order of tasks.
Do not pay for a job offer, background check or equipment sent by an unknown recruiter. Verify the employer independently.
CareerSource specialist services

entries.title: Florida identification card for a person who is homeless
entries.description:
Florida can waive the identification-card fee when a local homeless shelter provides the required letter verifying homelessness. Identity and lawful-presence documents are still required.
Camillus House lists help registering for a Florida ID. Ask staff to check your exact document list before a licensing-office visit.
Florida driver and identification handbook

entries.title: Replace a Social Security card
entries.description:
Social Security: 1-800-772-1213, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.
Replacement is free. Start online if eligible; otherwise arrange an appointment and ask which original documents are accepted. The card is mailed and is not normally issued the same day.
Social Security replacement-card steps

entries.title: Legal Services of Greater Miami
entries.description:
Phone: 305-576-0080.
Free civil legal help for eligible low-income residents of Miami-Dade and Monroe counties, including housing and public-benefit problems. Call for screening; representation is not guaranteed.
Legal Services of Greater Miami
entries.address: Address: 4343 W Flagler Street, Suite 100, Miami, FL 33134

entries.title: Office of New Americans
entries.description:
Phone: 305-636-1010.
Immigration legal-service referrals, naturalization support and connections for newly arrived residents. Call for the current free-consultation schedule.
Office of New Americans contact
entries.address: Address: Accion Community Center, 970 SW 1st Street, Suite 304, Miami, FL 33130

entries.title: Avoid immigration-service fraud
entries.description:
Only an authorised lawyer or accredited representative may give immigration legal advice. In the United States, a notary public is not automatically an immigration lawyer.
For suspicious or improper services, use the County Consumer Mediation Center. Do not hand over original identity documents without understanding why they are needed.
Miami-Dade immigration-service complaints

entries.title: Safe mailing address
entries.description:
Camillus House provides mail service. Before using it on benefit, court or employment forms, ask how to format the address, how often to check, what identification is required and when unclaimed mail is returned.
Update agencies when your mailing arrangement changes; missing a letter can close a benefit case or cause a court deadline to pass.
Camillus House mail service

categories.title: Women, youth, LGBTQ+ people, veterans and other groups

entries.title: Domestic violence
entries.description:
Florida Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-500-1119, 24 hours. National hotline: 1-800-799-SAFE (7233).
Ask for safety planning and confidential shelter options. Do not go to a confidential address without instructions. If the person causing harm is nearby or danger is immediate, call 911.
Lotus House domestic-violence contacts

entries.title: Pridelines — LGBTQ+ support
entries.description:
Phone: 305-571-9601.
LGBTQ+-affirming youth, adult and senior programs, mental-health support, health navigation and social connection. The current centre serves youth and young adults ages 13–24. Call to identify the right program; it is not an emergency shelter.
Pridelines current programs
entries.address: Miami Beach: 1130 Washington Avenue, 1st floor, Miami Beach, FL 33139

entries.title: The Trevor Project — LGBTQ+ young people in crisis
entries.description:
Call: 1-866-488-7386; text: START to 678678.
Confidential crisis counselling for LGBTQ+ young people. For immediate physical danger or a medical emergency, call 911.
The Trevor Project crisis services

entries.title: Homeless veterans
entries.description:
National Call Center for Homeless Veterans: 877-424-3838, free and confidential, 24 hours.
Connects veterans who are homeless or at imminent risk with local VA housing, health, treatment, employment and document support. A family member or neighbour may also call.
Miami VA homeless-veteran care

entries.title: Miami Vet Center
entries.description:
Phone: 305-718-3712; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. After hours: 877-927-8387.
Confidential counselling and referrals for eligible veterans, service members and families. Many services accept walk-ins; call if you are unsure about documents or eligibility.
Miami Vet Center
entries.address: Address: 8280 NW 27th Street, Suite 511, Miami, FL 33122

entries.title: Human trafficking or forced labour
entries.description:
National Human Trafficking Hotline: 888-373-7888; text 233733.
For forced work, commercial sexual exploitation, threats, withheld documents or control by a trafficker. The Homeless Helpline also routes domestic-violence and trafficking callers through option 2. Do not confront the suspected trafficker yourself.
National Human Trafficking Hotline

entries.title: People who need medical help during evacuation
entries.description:
Miami-Dade's Emergency & Evacuation Assistance Program is for residents who need specialised transportation, medical monitoring or help in an evacuation shelter. Registration should happen before a storm.
Call 311 or 305-468-5900 and explain mobility, equipment, medication, caregiver and transport needs. Registration does not replace 911 in an emergency.
Emergency & Evacuation Assistance Program

entries.title: Language access
entries.description:
Ask 311, 211, 988, hospitals and benefits offices for an interpreter. Miami-Dade 311 offers English, Spanish and Haitian Creole; other services may use telephone interpretation.
Do not sign a form you cannot understand. Ask for a copy and, for legal or immigration matters, use a qualified interpreter rather than an unknown intermediary.
Miami-Dade 311 language access

entries.title: Tell shelter access staff about the pet
entries.description:
Tell the Homeless Helpline about every animal before accepting a referral. Ask whether the animal can stay with you and what safe alternative exists if not. Rules differ by site and no listing here guarantees pet accommodation.
Do not abandon or surrender an animal based only on a verbal promise of a bed.
Miami-Dade Homeless Trust

entries.title: Humane Society Community Pet Pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 305-696-0800; pantry listed daily, 9:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.
May provide up to two weeks of pet food or supplies such as carriers, crates and leashes. Items depend on donations, so call before travelling.
Community Pet Support and Pantry
entries.address: Soffer and Fine Adoption Center: 16101 W Dixie Highway, North Miami Beach, FL 33160

entries.title: Miami-Dade Animal Services Wellness Clinic
entries.description:
Phone: 311 or 305-468-5900. Vaccinations are walk-in; sterilisation requires an appointment.
Low-cost vaccines and preventive care are available. People receiving specified public benefits may qualify for lower prices and must bring current proof; identification may be required to confirm pet ownership.
Animal Services vaccination and low-income fees
entries.address: Address: 3599 NW 79th Avenue, Doral, FL 33122

entries.title: Financial help for veterinary care
entries.description:
The Humane Society lists limited assistance for qualifying Miami-Dade pet owners, including some free or reduced-cost spay and neuter programs. Proof of financial hardship may be required and funds can run out.
Call before scheduling and ask what service, animal, ZIP code and documents qualify.
Humane Society financial-assistance programs

entries.title: Verification and corrections
entries.description:
This page uses Miami-Dade County, City of Miami, Florida and federal sources, plus the official websites of each listed provider. Exact times are included only where a current source publishes them; calling first is still recommended.
Found a closed service, wrong number or missing source of help? See how to contribute or submit a correction on GitHub. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
